result.title: ASIWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in a Persistent Survival Sandbox
result.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Project website: https://asigameworld.github.io/
result.summary: Evaluating autonomous agents requires examining whether they can translate goals into coherent action across extended interactions. In persistent environments, this requires coordinating interdependent actions under incomplete observations, accounting for delayed effects, and adapting as earlier decisions shape subsequent opportunities. We introduce ASIWorld, a survival sandbox that combines persistent world and character state with character-scoped observations and a programmable asynchronous interface to study sustained goal execution. Agents pursue interdependent production and exploration tasks through direct actions or agent-authored programs that continue running between model calls. The evaluation assesses task success, the attainment of development achievements, and survival costs, complemented by an analysis of execution behavior. In an exploratory study of nine agent configurations using a common harness, eight complete the production task and six complete both tasks. Analyses of execution trajectories and performance across difficulty levels reveal different preparation, combat, and recovery behaviors among configurations with similar task outcomes. Incomplete preparation is associated with stalled progression, while configurations that complete the tasks differ in survival costs and the fulfillment of additional achievement criteria. These findings illustrate the value of assessing sustained goal execution through both task outcomes and the behaviors and costs associated with achieving them.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ASIWorld：一个持久化世界与角色状态的生存沙盒基准，让智能体在部分观测、延迟效应和相互依赖的任务（生产与探索）中执行长期目标，并以任务成功、成就达成和生存成本及执行轨迹来评估，对九种智能体配置做了探索性研究。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准关注部分观测下的持久状态、延迟效应与跨模型调用的持续程序，可能为 LVR 中跨调用维持的推理状态、状态抽象与停止/成本决策提供问题表述上的启发；但全文未涉及视觉表征或 latent 推理，联系需较多核查。
